title: SuperScout verified handoff record
description: One gated handoff, as released (one object per JSONL line). SuperScout-7B ends its search episode by emitting a handoff document: a <files>/<repro>/<notes> tagged text block terminated by STOP. The verify-then-strip gate replays the document's reproduction claim in the task sandbox at the base commit and strips the <repro> block when the claim does not hold; this record carries the (possibly stripped) document plus the gate's verification record.

task_id.description: Benchmark instance identifier of the task the handoff belongs to.

handoff_type.description: How the handoff was obtained: 'spontaneous' = the model emitted it on its own; 'forced' = at turn-budget exhaustion one extra generation demanded the handoff in-dialect. Forced handoffs are tagged and never pooled with spontaneous ones in find-rate claims.

handoff_text_final.description: The handoff document AFTER the gate ran: identical to the emitted document when the reproduction claim verified (or there was nothing to verify), with the entire <repro> block removed when the claim was false.

failure_class.description: Diagnostic label attached by the gate driver, classifying WHY the replayed command failed (or why nothing ran) from the captured output: 'real_failure' = genuine bug reproduction (traceback / assertion / failed test); 'missing_file' / 'import_error' = setup error, not a bug demonstration; 'nonzero_other' = non-zero exit with unclassified output; 'passed_stripped' = command exited 0, so the claim was false and the <repro> block was stripped; 'no_repro' / 'claim_not_true' / 'no_command' / 'not_run' = nothing was verified. Only a clean exit-0 pass strips.

handoffDocument.description: The handoff wire format: raw unescaped text (NOT JSON) in three XML-style tag blocks, ending with the token STOP on its own line. <files>: implicated files, ranked, one path per line. <repro> (optional; absent after a strip): three fields on 'key:' lines — 'command:' the exact command that reproduces the failure (the value may span multiple lines and is read until the next 'reproduced:'/'observed:' field), 'reproduced:' true if the observed output demonstrates the bug, otherwise false, 'observed:' the failing output observed before any fix. <notes>: free prose (findings, dead ends, build/test quirks). Consumers extract per-field, so one broken tag does not invalidate the document. The format specification caps the document at 4KB total (enforced upstream when handoffs are produced and trimmed); the gate itself does not reject oversized documents, and released records may slightly exceed the cap.

allOf.description: A handoff document contains a <files> block.
A handoff document ends with the token STOP (trailing whitespace allowed).

verifyRecord.description: The record returned by verify_strip.verify_and_strip for this handoff: what was parsed out of the <repro> block, whether the command was replayed in the sandbox, and the keep/strip outcome.

has_repro.description: True if the document contained a <repro>...</repro> block.

command.description: The reproduction command extracted from the block's 'command:' field; null if absent.

claim.description: The parsed 'reproduced:' value (true/yes -> true); null if the field is missing.

ran.description: True if the gate actually executed the command in the sandbox (only done for claim == true with a command present).

returncode.description: Exit code of the replayed command; null if it never ran.

verified.description: Gate verdict: true if the command failed as claimed (non-zero exit, or a failure-substring hint when hints are enabled); false if it passed; null if it never ran.

stripped.description: True if the <repro> block was removed from the forwarded handoff.

reason.description: Why the gate kept or stripped: 'verified_reproduces' = claim true and the command failed (kept, verified); 'claim_false_repro_passes' = claim true but the command exited 0 (stripped); the other three = nothing to verify (kept unchanged, never run).

output_tail.description: Last 1000 characters of the replayed command's output. Present only when the command ran.
